feedback: John found revision 01 insufficiently adventurous and specifically requested text spilling across areas, as in Grow Easy. He supplied the exact Grow Easy image URL and asked that it be used as a seed alongside T05.
prompt:
Design ONE adventurous, sophisticated front cover for the UK gardening book "The Vegetable Guru", using BOTH supplied images as direct creative references. Complete cover as ONE image, finished lettering and photo composition together. Flat artwork only, portrait 185:240 aspect ratio, no 3D book mock-up.

Image 1 is the author's ORIGINAL photograph: John Lennon holding a colander of ripe tomatoes in his greenhouse. This is the subject/identity reference. Preserve his recognisable real face, age, thinning grey hair, grey beard, gentle expression, checked shirt, olive T-shirt, natural hands and tomato harvest. Keep it photographic, not illustrated or artificially beautified. His face and the whole bowl must remain unobstructed and clearly readable. Use an upper-body crop and the rich original foliage. Background can be extended for this composition, but retain the greenhouse setting.

Image 2 is the exact "Grow Easy" cover by Anna Greenland, published by Mitchell Beazley. This is the primary GRAPHIC COMPOSITION reference, not merely a colour swatch. Study how its giant fine serif letters begin OUTSIDE the photograph on the yellow surround and continue over the photograph, how the frame is an active graphic field, how different scales and alignments create editorial tension. The user specifically wants those adventurous graphic devices, not another framed portrait with headings tidily contained inside it. Use its design intelligence to make an original cover. Do not copy its words, endorsement circle, author or publisher text.

Commit to this strong composition:
- A FLAT matte warm ochre/marigold-yellow canvas, no gradient, glows or shaded frame.
- An OFF-CENTRE portrait photographic window, noticeably shifted RIGHT, leaving a broad yellow strip on the LEFT. Roughly its left edge sits at 18-22% of the cover width, its top at 15-20% of cover height, right edge nearly at the outer right edge, lower edge around 88%. The result should be visibly asymmetrical, not a centered photo with equal margins.
- Recompose the greenhouse portrait so John's head occupies the right-hand middle, below the large title; his bowl of red tomatoes is substantial in the lower half. Create enough natural leafy space above and to his left for the lettering.
- The TITLE must make a bold graphic move across the photograph's left edge. Start "Vegetable" out on the yellow LEFT FIELD, let its enormous V straddle the yellow/photo boundary, and continue the rest of the word across the photograph. The word must remain fully readable. This crossing is essential.
- Place "Guru" as another very large, confident, differently indented line: its sweeping G begins on the yellow field and crosses into the leafy photograph, with a graceful descender returning into the yellow field. Position this to the LEFT of John's clear face. The title should feel woven through the composition, not centered above a picture.
- Use warm cream, high-contrast editorial serif display lettering, beautifully spaced, with elegant broad curves and a few expressive swashes. Make the varied scale of "The", "Vegetable" and "Guru" intentional. "The" is small and tucked neatly into the title's negative space, not a separate banner.
- Let ONE or TWO real photographic leaves subtly cross the lower-left boundary of the photographic window onto the yellow field, creating a restrained second layer of depth. Keep any overlap away from the exact words and the person; no decorative illustration.
- Supporting typography is modest and refined. Set the subtitle as a small readable two-line block in a carefully chosen quiet area of the yellow field, preferably lower left rather than a giant full-width strip at the top. Author name sits on the lower yellow field, left-aligned or offset to suit the composition, smaller than in the earlier design and secondary to the title. Use deep forest green for these supporting words.

Keep the palette disciplined: flat warm yellow, warm cream, dark forest green, natural leafy greens and red tomatoes. The interior is a friendly, colourful illustrated reference book with cream pages and strong rounded headings; the cover can be more expressive and editorial without looking cold or academic. Bold hierarchy, confident negative space, photographic authenticity, sophisticated contemporary bookshop quality. This is a gardening BOOK, not a video thumbnail or advertising poster. Do not add badges, pull quotes, icons, borders around individual text blocks, flourishes unrelated to the letterforms, drop shadows, bevels, artificial sunbeams, extra slogans or logos.

EXACT TEXT, each once:
The Vegetable Guru
Your at-a-glance growing companion
John Lennon

No other text. The title can use expressive line breaks but do not split an individual word or lose a letter. Fully legible text with no text over the face, hands or bowl. Generate a single complete, strongly art-directed front cover with the title visibly spilling from yellow into the image.
